Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Energy Corporation Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Energy Corporation's Q2 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Mike Harlan, Chief Executive Officer; John Ramirez, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Operating Officer; and David Patel, VP of Exploration.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we make today may be forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

I will now turn the call over to Mike Harlan.

Mike Harlan: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Apex Energy Corporation delivered solid results in Q2 2024, driven by strong operational performance and favorable commodity prices. We saw meaningful growth in production volumes, with total output, oil, and gas showing solid quarter-over-quarter and year-over-year gains across our key basins. Our midstream operations posted resilient performance, with elevated transportation volumes and steady progress on infrastructure builds. EBITDA climbed sharply year-over-year, powered by higher volumes, better pricing, and tight cost controls. We also continued to drive down operating expenses per BOE through targeted efficiencies. I'm particularly pleased with our progress on capital expenditure guidance, maintaining a disciplined approach to future spending with strong projected returns. We are focused on high-grading our inventory and executing short-cycle projects. Further, we are advancing low-carbon initiatives and portfolio optimization. Finally, we are taking steps to deleverage while returning capital to shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to John Ramirez to discuss our financial results in more detail.

John Ramirez: Thank you, Mike, and good morning, everyone. As Mike highlighted, we had a strong quarter across the board. Our revenue reached $6.8 billion, up 20% year-over-year, reflecting higher realized prices and volume growth. Operating income stood at $2.4 billion, while net income came in at $1.7 billion. We generated $1.3 billion in free cash flow and returned $450 million to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases. Our balance sheet remains rock-solid, with $12 billion in long-term debt and $3.2 billion in cash and equivalents, keeping net debt to EBITDA at a comfortable 1.2 times.

Let me dive deeper into the key drivers starting with our production volumes, which form the foundation of our value creation. We prioritize high-margin, oil-weighted assets mainly in the Permian Basin, supplemented by Eagle Ford and our expanding Gulf of Mexico positions. Despite seasonal maintenance, supply chain challenges, and fluctuating prices—WTI at $82 per barrel on average and Henry Hub gas around $2.80 per MMBtu—our operations hit 255,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day in Q2. That breaks down to 185,000 barrels of oil per day and 70,000 BOE per day from natural gas, based on 420,000 Mcf per day at our standard 6:1 factor. This disciplined focus directed 65% of our drilling and completion budget to oil-rich intervals, optimizing cash flows in this strong crude environment.

Quarter-over-quarter, total production rose 6% from Q1's 240,000 BOE per day—185,000 oil and 55,000 gas equivalent—with oil jumping 9% thanks to new Delaware Basin pads in the Permian. Those 12 fresh Wolfcamp A and B horizontals, averaging 12,000 feet, featured advanced fracs with 4,500 pounds of proppant per foot. Initial productions topped 1,200 BOE per day, 85% oil, and 30-day rates beat our type curves by 15%. Gas held flat due to intentional Eagle Ford curtailments to boost NGL capture amid soft local pricing, influenced by Haynesville constraints like those at Enterprise. We did experience a brief drop from Eagle Ford Pearsall turnarounds, shutting 15,000 BOE per day for gas plant upgrades, but volumes have rebounded to 95% of prior levels.

Year-over-year, we're ahead 16% from last Q2's 220,000 BOE per day—160,000 oil and 60,000 gas—with oil up 16% on a $1.2 billion Midland Basin acquisition adding 20,000 barrels per day of stable legacy output, akin to ConocoPhillips' add-ons. Gas climbed 17%, capturing full-year benefits from 2023 Permian Black Shale infills using existing infrastructure for 25% faster cycles via simul-fracs.

By region, Permian accounted for 70% of the advance at 180,000 BOE per day, up 10% QoQ and 20% YoY with 80% oil mix. Northern Delaware shines via geochemical insights into a Second Bone Spring bench, matching Pioneer benchmarks at 1.2 million BOE per well estimated ultimate recovery. Eagle Ford steady at 45,000 BOE per day, down 5% QoQ on upkeep but up 8% YoY, shifting to oilier Austin Chalk amid gas glut. Gulf of Mexico at 30,000 BOE per day, up 12% QoQ post-Lucius tie-backs reaching capacity, echoing Chevron's Anchor.

This oil tilt—73% of BOE now, from 70% last year—sets us up for robust free cash flow. We've hedged 60% of Q3 and Q4 oil at $78 per barrel, with 20% of capex in low-carbon efforts like electrified fracs and Pecos carbon capture, tapping IRA benefits. Q3 guidance is 260,000 to 270,000 BOE per day, Permian pads lifting another 15,000, barring weather like Uri.

Shifting to adjusted EBITDA, we posted $3.2 billion, a healthy 22% rise from $2.6 billion in Q2 2023—our best since late 2022. Volumes drove about 45% of that, or $270 million, with 525,000 BOE per day average, 12% above last year's 468,000. Permian accelerated with 28 Delaware horizontals at 12,500 feet, IP rates over 1,800 BOE per day using ceramic proppants from CARBO Ceramics. Oil mix hit 68% from 65%, on $80-plus WTI.

U.S. onshore, led by Permian and Eagle Ford, fueled 65% of volume gains, Permian at record 320,000 BOE per day up 18% YoY via pad efficiencies and SLB's DrillOps. Gulf's Lucius added 15,000 BOE per day despite Beryl downtime; North Sea lagged on UK taxes but NCS offset with 5% from Johan Sverdrup infills.

Realized pricing contributed 30% or $180 million: oil at $76.50 per barrel, up 12% from $68.20, on tight WTI-Brent at $3.50 and Europe refining. NGLs at $28 equivalent from $22, Mont Belvieu at $18 spreads. Hedged 65% Q3 oil at $72 floor against NYMEX swings.

Costs added 25% or $210 million, OpEx per BOE down 8% to $18.50 from $20.10. But let's zoom in on operating expenses per BOE specifically, our key efficiency gauge covering LOE, G&T, workovers, taxes, and handling—separate from DD&A and G&A. It shapes breakevens at $42 per BOE company-wide, under Pioneer's post-Exxon range.

Over five quarters, OpEx per BOE fell from $14.20 peak in Q4 2023 to $10.45 now—a 26% YoY drop, 8% sequential, lowest since 2019. Q4 2023 spiked on Permian weather LOE to $8.50, chemical inflation, services; G&T to $3.40. Q1 eased to $11.35 with Cost Zero LOE at $7.10, G&T $2.80 post-Matterhorn plant. Q2 at $10.45: LOE $6.40 down 25% YoY, G&T $2.50, workovers $0.75—better than Chevron's Permian $11-12 or Conoco's $13 blended.

Permian $8.90 down 22% on scale/tech; Eagle Ford $11.20 down 18% condensate focus; Bakken $13.50 down 15% water handling; Gulf $18.75 down 10% deferred work. Permian anchors via drilling scale near hubs.

This stems from strategies targeting 10-15% cuts yearly to sub-$9 by 2026. Tech drives 40%: Delfi AI cut downtime 30%, $0.80/BOE LOE save; digital twins extend ESPs to 24 months; 50 drones slash inspections to $0.15/BOE; Oxy robotic interventions. Ops 30%: bio-inhibitors down chemicals 18%; Bakken water recycle to $0.90/BOE; workovers down 22% high-ROI only. Midstream/supply 20%: Enterprise take-or-pay $0.45/MMBtu; Waha stake saves $0.60; Halliburton discounts. Regional 10%: Permian growth to 350,000 BOE per day; Bakken divest $200 million to Eagle Ford; diesel hedges $2.80/gal.

Margins hit 52% from 45%, first-quartile $28 D&C Permian. Q3 $10.00-10.30 per BOE, $9.50 FY2025, risks hurricanes or regs.

Back to EBITDA, non-recurs added $120 million: $75 million Gulf insurance, $45 million Bakken impairment reversals at $75 WTI SEC. Amid 5% rig drop, our inventory shines; $2.8 billion upstream capex 70% Permian, Oxy CCUS pilots for $4 billion annual FCF at $70 Brent, $1.5 billion returns, 3.2% yield.

Our midstream segment bolstered this, yielding $1.2 billion adjusted EBITDA, up 18% YoY and 5% QoQ, via record throughput and project execution. Assets include 12,000 pipeline miles, 150 million barrel storage, fractionation, rail in Permian, Bakken, Haynesville.

Crude transport 1.85 million barrels per day, up 14% YoY 3% QoQ, Permian 1.1 million up 22% on 6.2 million basin output despite Cactus II issues. Utilization 88% overall, 95% Permian like Apex Permian Express, akin Enterprise no discounts. Gas 3.2 Bcf per day up 11% Haynesville ramp; NGL 450,000 barrels per day Mont Belvieu expansions like Targa. Bakken 250,000 crude differentials $1.50; Trans Mountain JV 50,000 Canadian heavy at $0.25 tolls.

Long-haul 65% under 10-year take-or-pay insulates; tariff $1.45 equivalent up 4% escalators. Minimal curtailment post-DUC drawdown.

Infrastructure: $2.8 billion 2024 capex 60% YTD. Apex Horizon 450-mile Waha-Gulf 800,000 barrels per day complete June, 75% committed Exxon/Oxy, $250 million EBITDA add Q3 at 300,000 initial flows erasing -$0.50 Waha discounts. Permian NGL +100,000 to 750,000 Pecos; Haynesville +500 MMcf/d Matterhorn. DAS fiber 40% lines cut leaks 70% like Kinder; drone ILI 85% saves $12 million opex. CCUS 2 million tons Fervo, 45Q.

Permian $1.5 billion queue incl EPIC reversal; Bakken rail units +40,000; Haynesville LNG support. Anchor-expand: 80-90% pre-FID. ROIC 12.5% to 15% 2026, 3.2x leverage. Contracts 7 years, 92% fee-based. Q3 EBITDA $1.3-1.4 billion, FY volumes +12-15%, 20% 2025 growth $4 billion backlog. Risks FERC, basis.

Wrapping financials, our capex guidance anchors disciplined allocation for superior returns in volatility. 2024 actual $3.6 billion at midpoint $3.4-3.8 billion, +8% from 2023, upstream Permian 145 D&C wells 12,000 feet average. Maintenance facilities, lifts at 92% efficiency. Returns: Permian 55% IRR $65 WTI, $35 half-cycle, 30%+ ROCE Tier 1.

2025 $4.1-4.5 billion midpoint +14%, 85% upstream on $70-75 Brent, $3-3.50 Henry Hub, low services. Upstream 70% $2.9-3.2 billion: Permian Delaware $2.1 billion 165 wells cube 48-pad, D&C $850/foot -12% YoY super-spec 2,500 lbs/foot diverters; 60% IRR payback <10 months 1.8 MBOE EUR; 20 CO2 EOR Oxy-like +15% recovery. Eagle Ford $500 million 40 Sligo $25 breakeven 45% IRR condensate LNG. GoM $400 million two Anchor tie-backs +25,000 BOE/d 2026 50%+ IRR.

Expl/appraisal 10% $400-450 million: $250 million two Namibia frontier Venus-like $1 billion NPV10 25% success; DJ Niobrara 20% IRR. Maintenance/infra 15% $600-700 million LOE flat $6/BOE: 40% Permian electrify -25% Scope 1 Delfi twins +15% injectivity net-zero 2050. Corporate 5% $200 million CCUS 50 MMcf/d 45Q IRA.

65% Permian 1.8 net/rig/year post-Diamondback; avoid Midland volatility 4,000 loc >50% IRR. Pause North Sea fiscal, redirect Middle East analogs. Returns-first 40% IRR $60 WTI, 20%+ FCF yield; $2.8 billion 2025 FCF $1.5 billion returns 3.2% dividend. To 2027 5% CAGR $4.8 billion +7% production 450 MBOE/d 0.5x debt/EBITDA. Energy security, LNG, AI gas; $800 million deferrable < $60 WTI.

I will now turn the call over to Lisa Chen for an operational update.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, John. Operationally, we're executing sharply. Production averaged 255,000 BOE per day, aligning with our oil-weighted strategy. We ramped Delaware Basin cube developments online, set to fuel near-term growth. Cost reductions continue via tech and scale, supporting low breakevens.

Now I'll turn it over to David Patel for exploration.

David Patel: Thank you, Lisa. Our exploration efforts hold tremendous promise. We finished seismic in offshore Namibia and plan two high-impact wells next year, akin to TotalEnergies' Venus, with multi-billion NPV potential. Domestically, DJ Basin Niobrara appraisal targets solid returns. These could materially expand reserves.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you provide more detail on production volumes quarter-over-quarter and year-over-year?

Mike Harlan: Good question, John. As John Ramirez outlined, we hit 255,000 BOE per day in Q2, up 6% QoQ and 16% YoY, led by Permian oil ramps and acquisitions. Details in the release show the drivers clearly.

Operator: Our next question comes from Lisa Wong with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Lisa Wong: Good morning. What are your expectations for capital expenditure plans and returns?

John Ramirez: Morning, Lisa. Our 2025 guidance of $4.1 to $4.5 billion targets 60% IRR hurdles, with Permian cube wells at payback under 10 months. Multi-year, it grows production 7% annually to 450,000 BOE per day while deleveraging sharply.

Operator: Our next question comes from Mike Patel with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Mike Patel: Could you please provide more color on operating expenses per BOE trends?

Lisa Chen: Hi Mike. We've driven OpEx to $10.45 per BOE, down 26% YoY via AI predictive tools, water recycling, and supply deals—targeting sub-$9 by 2026 across regions.

Operator: Our next question comes from Sarah Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Sarah Lee: How will the results of the exploration program affect the company's future strategy?

David Patel: Great point, Sarah. Success in Namibia or DJ could add billions in NPV, shifting more capex to appraisal and high-grading inventory, enhancing our 4,000-location Permian queue while diversifying offshore.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the conference back over to Mike Harlan for closing remarks.

Mike Harlan: Thank you, Operator. In summary, we are pleased with our performance in Q2 2024. We remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering value to our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
